newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up in thin volume as soybeans rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up in thin volume as soybeans rally.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher, lifted by a rally in soybeans, traders said.
But the volume was light and gains were capped by nearly ideal crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, they said.
USDA Monday confirmed the U.S. crop was in satisfactory shape and pegged the corn condition at 65 percent good to excellent, above the 60 percent in that category the previous week.
Warmer temperatures this week should further boost U.S. corn crop ratings, the traders said.
Slow farmer selling was cited as were spreads.

Bull spreading contributed to advances in the July with Griffin Trading doing four million bushels of July/December and Merrill Lynch Futures spread two million bushels of July/December, traders said.

But Cargill Inc took the other side of the spread and did four million December/July and also was a featured seller of four million July outright and sold 3.5 million bushels of September, traders said.
Corn closed unchanged to 3/4 cent per bushel higher with July up 3/4 at $2.72-1/2. December closed steady at $2.55-1/2.
Traders said the market, particularly the soybean market, found support from a strengthening El Nino weather pattern.

A U.S. official said Tuesday warm ocean temperatures off the western coast of South America have triggered an El Nino weather pattern that could have a significant impact on crop production around the world.
Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million bushels of July, Dean Witter Reynolds bought 1.5 million July and sold two million July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000 contracts, below the 58,387 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Tenco Inc sold 500 July $2.70 calls at 4-3/4 to 5-1/2 cents, Term Commodities bought 500 July $2.70 calls at 4-3/4 cents and LIT America bought 250 July $3.10 calls at 1/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 13,643 traded Tuesday.
